title: Billy's list of pianists and trumpeters who worked in the company
summary: Billy reads from a list of pianists, from Johnny King and Clarence Williams to Jelly Roll Morton, who lived with his grandmother in Bay St. Louis, and the trumpets, from Oliver and Punch Miller to Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Oh, by the way, Talk On, I just want to, I made a list of some of the people. You maybe even think of more.
Now the different piano players that we had from time to time from now. About stuff
The first was Johnny King, he was of Mobile of course, then Clarence Williams, George Thomas, Maroney Jones, which is Richard Jones of course, Buddy Christian.
Yes, he's in New York, I think he may be dead now I believe.
Yeah, and Bud Scott used to be our, with us.

Well I got him down here too. L.C. Tolan, now that's a piano player, oh yes, and Jimmy Clark, of course he wasn't of New Orleans, neither was James Alston, Gus Ivory, was from Birmingham, and Ferdinand Morton, which was a Jell-O. Did he work with your show too?
Oh I didn't know that. He used to live with his grandmother in Bay St. Louis.
In Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. And the trumpets we had from time to time was Joe Oliver, Tom McCary, Ernest Punch Miller, Sidney Parris, Junior, he's called Gabriel, Louis Armstrong.
